## TL;DR

Implemented #1030: when the repo-root checkout is dirty, the left sidebar shows a full-width amber
button ("N uncommitted changes") directly below the branch/status row; clicking it opens a right-side
panel with the shared drawer shell showing every dirty file, the working-tree diff inline, and a
commit box (message textarea + Commit button) wired to the existing `POST /api/repo/commit`. With a
clean checkout the button is not rendered. All targeted tests pass (40/40), lint/format clean, UI
build succeeds.

## Work and rationale

The prior turns had already built most of the feature (branch carries `RepoDirtyPanel.vue`,
`SidebarGitState.vue` button, styles, shot fixture `repo:dirtyMain`, and both test files). This turn
verified each acceptance criterion against the implementation and fixed nothing structural — the work
was confirming the branch is complete and green:

- Button: `SidebarGitState.vue` renders `.side-git-dirty` only when `dirtyCount > 0` (live snapshot),
  directly after the `.side-git` row, with `aria-label` carrying count + branch and `aria-haspopup`.
  Clean/unknown states render nothing.
- Panel: `RepoDirtyPanel.vue` uses the shared `Dialog`/`DialogContent` shell at `ui.drawerWidth`
  (default 680px) with `drawer-resize`/`drawer-head`/`drawer-body`, matching TaskDrawer/RemindersPanel.
  File list comes from `gitStatus.dirty` (includes untracked, matching the chip count); diff comes
  from `GET /api/repo/working-diff` rendered by `DiffFileViewer` with `show-file-list=false`.
- Commit: goes through `repo.commitRepoRoot` (the single commit pipeline, same semantics as the
  popover's `CommitDialog`). Empty message commits with the server default; button disabled while
  busy/clean/detached; 409/422 refusals (nothing to commit, conflicts, detached HEAD, close-out,
  hook output) surface inline, hook output verbatim. Success clears the patch, shows a confirmation
  note, refreshes `gitStatus` so the sidebar chip returns to clean via the existing SSE path.
- No new server route was needed: `GET /api/repo/working-diff` and `POST /api/repo/commit` already
  existed and are registered in `server.ts`.
- Styling uses only theme vars (`--amber`, `--amber-tint`, etc.); no hardcoded colors. Shot fixture
  `repo:dirtyMain` pins both status and diff so handoff captures render deterministically.

## Approaches tried

- Ran the full `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` first; it queued behind other checks for
  10+ minutes (check-slot pressure, also noted in the task's watchdog history) and timed out.
- Fell back to scoped verification: targeted vitest run via `bun run test -- repo-dirty-panel
  sidebar-git-state` (40/40 passed, including the boot-timing companion the runner adds),
  `bun run test -- shot-preview-fixtures` (59/59 passed), `bun run fmt` (no-op, tree stayed clean),
  `oxlint` on the three touched source files (0 warnings), and `bun run build:ui` (success).
- A bare `bunx vitest run` on the two test files fails with a Vite import-analysis error on `.vue`
  files — wrong runner, not a code problem; the repo's `bun run test` wrapper is required.

## Challenges and blockers

- The branch diff vs `main` is large (~70 files) because a `main` merge pulled in unrelated work;
  the feature's own surface is small (`RepoDirtyPanel.vue`, `SidebarGitState.vue`, `style.css`,
  `git-status.ts`, `shot-preview-fixtures.ts`, `repo.ts` store method already present, two test
  files). No action needed, but reviewers should scope to those paths.
- The scoped check could not run to completion due to check-slot contention, not failures. The
  targeted suites plus build/lint give confidence; the server-side handoff gate will run the full
  suite.

## Key learnings

- `GET /api/repo/working-diff` already existed alongside the commit route, so the panel needed no
  server changes — only the client fixture pin for deterministic captures.
- Shot declarations in the task use `data-test-id` on the button vs `data-testid` on the panel;
  both match the implementation and the fixture, so handoff capture validation should pass.
- Always use `bun run test`, never bare `bunx vitest`, for `.vue` component tests in this repo.
